15224.one_liner: A three-hour documentary following legendary Hungarian director Béla Tarr as he runs a filmmaking workshop with students in Fukushima, Japan.
15224.long_desc: Directed by Kaori Oda, one of Tarr's first students at his Film Factory school in Sarajevo, this documentary portrait observes Tarr teaching and mentoring young filmmakers on location in disaster-affected Fukushima. It follows the process of developing student film projects, showing Tarr's approach to storytelling, location scouting, and building tension in scenes. Oda's earlier films (Aragane, Toward a Common Tenderness, Cenote) premiered at Rotterdam and DOK Leipzig, and she won the 2020 Nagisa Oshima Award. Runtime is a full 180 minutes (3 hours).

15183.one_liner: An observational documentary covering the 167-day trial of Hungarian right-wing extremists accused of murdering Roma people in 2008-2009.
15183.long_desc: Director Eszter Hajdú's crew filmed the entire courtroom process of a case in which six Roma people were killed and four suspects stood trial. The film scrutinizes the prejudices voiced by witnesses, lawyers, and a notably severe judge, raising the question of who is really on trial - the murderers or their victims. It won 19 international awards and screened in over 40 countries. Runtime 108 minutes; a Q&A follows the screening.

15079.one_liner: A 16mm documentary essay about Cao Thị Hậu, one of the last members of Vietnam's Rục ethnic minority, preserving her people's language and stories for her grandson.
15079.long_desc: Shot on grainy Bolex 16mm film by directors Nicolas Graux and Minh Quý Truong, the film follows an isolated Vietnamese minority community forced to abandon its traditional way of life after first contact with the outside world in the 1960s. Water and impermanence run through the film as visual metaphors for the erosion of collective memory. It centers on grandparenting and caregiving as ways cultural knowledge survives. The film won the Golden Leopard (Filmmakers of the Present) at Locarno 2025 and the Main Prize at BAFICI 2026.

15241.one_liner: A German drama about a long-distance millennial couple - a writer and a web designer - who keep pulling toward and away from each other between Berlin and a small town near Frankfurt.
15241.long_desc: Adapted by director Anna Roller from Leif Randt's novel (Randt also wrote the screenplay), the film follows Tanja and Jerome as their relationship plays out through long messages, train journeys, and visits. When Tanja panics about commitment around her 34th birthday, a website Jerome designed becomes a metaphor for the routines threatening their relationship. It's shot with a deliberately controlled color palette to mirror the characters' moods. The film follows Roller's earlier Dead Girls Dancing (shown at this festival in 2023) and contains strobe lighting. A Q&A follows the screening.

15308.one_liner: An Austrian tragicomedy about a cold, work-obsessed Viennese businessman forced to confront mortality and reconsider his life after a serious diagnosis.
15308.long_desc: Directed by Marie Kreutzer (her second feature) and adapted from Doris Knecht's novel, the film follows Johannes Gruber, a narcissistic corporate executive estranged from his family, who meets DJ Sara on a business trip in Switzerland and feels an unexpected connection. Shortly after, he's diagnosed with a serious illness that pushes him to search for meaning. The film mixes drama with romantic comedy. It won Best Cinematography at Austria's Romy awards and Best Music at the Beijing International Film Festival, both in 2015. Part of the festival's Marie Kreutzer retrospective.

15114.one_liner: A US drama in which Chris Pine plays a divorced doctor in Cleveland who reconnects with his high school sweetheart, played by Jenny Slate, now returned to town.
15114.long_desc: Director Rachel Lambert, filming in her own hometown, follows Noah, who runs his late father's medical practice and cares for his anxious daughter, as his path crosses again with Rebecca. Both have changed since their teenage years, and a pivotal confrontation forces them to reckon with old emotional patterns and mutual shortcomings. The film centers on second chances and whether love is worth the complications it brings. Supporting cast includes Abby Ryder Fortson, Sam Waterston, and Katey Sagal.

15049.tytulPl: Nie ma duchów w mieszkaniu na Dobrej
15049.tytulOrg: Nie ma duchów w mieszkaniu na Dobrej
15049.one_liner: A Polish debut feature about four neurotic adult siblings who have an unspoken pact to look after each other, until one of them breaks it.
15049.long_desc: Director Emi Buchwald's debut feature follows Jana, Franek, Nastka, and Benek, whose mutual dependence is upended when one sibling challenges their long-standing arrangement, forcing all four to renegotiate their relationships. The film has a loose, episodic structure and naturalistic dialogue, drawing comparisons to J.D. Salinger. It won Best Director at the 2025 Gdynia Festival of Polish Feature Films along with several other awards, including the Złoty Pazur (Andrzej Żuławski Award). A Q&A follows the screening.

15195.one_liner: A programme of six new Polish short films from the festival's Shortlista selection, running about 71 minutes total.
15195.long_desc: This block screens six recent Polish short films together: "Długa przerwa" (dir. Jan Saczek), about a teacher whose accidentally-sent intimate photos spiral into a scandal; "Lato gładkiego asfaltu" (dir. Maria Dakszewicz); "Niech zostanie bez tytułu" (dir. Mieszko Chomka); "Skrawki" (dir. Olga Papacz); "Spiritus sanctus" (dir. Michał Toczek); and "Trakcje" (dir. Jakub Krzyszpin). "Długa przerwa" won the Narrative Student Short award at Austin Film Festival 2025 and the Manifest Award at Poitiers Film Festival 2025. A Q&A follows the screening.

15357.one_liner: A Spanish drama in which Javier Bardem plays a renowned, controversial filmmaker who casts his estranged daughter in the lead role of his new desert film project.
15357.long_desc: Directed by Rodrigo Sorogoyen, the film follows Esteban Martínez as he returns to Spain after years working in America to shoot an ambitious film in the desert, casting his daughter Emilía (a supporting actress) in a role that draws criticism from the industry and doubt from Emilía herself. Under the pressure of the shoot and the desert heat, old resentments and guilt resurface between father and daughter. Sorogoyen previously won multiple Goya Awards for Best Director and Screenplay for The Kingdom and Beasts. Cast includes Victoria Luengo, Raúl Arévalo, and Marina Foïs.

15242.one_liner: A French drama about a young woman, Louise, whose grief and vivid imagination blur the line between a real romance and one she may be inventing.
15242.long_desc: Director Isabel Pagliai's film follows Louise as she writes, walks, and grieves the disappearance of a man named Anton, uncertain whether he will return or ever existed. When a man named Thomas appears and their relationship develops entirely in forest settings, the film keeps it ambiguous whether he is real or a projection of her longing for connection. It's a coming-of-age story about loneliness and imagination as both refuge and a way of experiencing love, more driven by mood and emotion than conventional plot. The film won Best Debut at FIDMarseille 2025.

15291.one_liner: A Chinese sci-fi epic by Bi Gan set in a future where humanity has eliminated dreaming (and mortality), except for a cursed few "Phantoms" who still dream and experience cinema.
15291.long_desc: Structured as five interlinked segments spanning different film styles and eras - expressionist silent film, wartime noir, a Buddhist parable, a neorealist heist, and a millennial vampire romance - the film is both a genre tour and a formal tribute to cinema history itself. It won the Special Jury Prize at Cannes 2025. Cast includes Jackson Yee, Shu Qi, and Mark Chao. At 159 minutes, it's one of the longer films in this time block.

15022.one_liner: A German animated family film (age 6+) about a young humpback whale who sets off to rescue his parents and stop a monster called Leviathan from destroying the ocean.
15022.long_desc: After losing his parents - his father was the legendary "Whale Singer" whose song protected the sea - Vincent discovers the dangerous creature Leviathan has escaped from melting ice and now threatens the underwater world. Accompanied by an overprotective remora fish named Walter and a brave orca named Darya, he journeys to the mystical Sea of Eternity to bring his parents back. The film touches on loss, self-belief, teamwork, and environmental protection. Directed by Reza Memari; part of the festival's Młode Horyzonty (Young Horizons) children's section.

15414.one_liner: A French semi-documentary-style drama following Shana, a chronically late, high-energy young woman navigating family conflict and a toxic ex through the Paris suburbs.
15414.long_desc: Director Lila Pinell shoots on 16mm with a loose, restless camera that follows Shana from one predicament to the next, using nervous editing to convey her mood swings and inner turbulence. Supported by close friends, Shana resists others' attempts to fix or judge her as she pushes back against family conflict and a toxic ex-boyfriend. The film treats its protagonist with compassion rather than moralizing. It won the SACD Prize at Cannes 2026 (Quinzaine des cinéastes); contains strobe lighting effects.

15083.tytulEn: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
15083.tytulOrg: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
15083.one_liner: Documentary revisiting a 1972 gathering of Harlem Renaissance-era writers, musicians and activists at Duke Ellington's home, filmed by William Greaves and completed decades later by his son.
15083.long_desc: In 1972, filmmaker William Greaves filmed a one-off reunion of prominent Harlem Renaissance figures - writers, musicians, actors and activists - at the home of Duke Ellington. The footage sat unfinished until his son David Greaves, who operated a camera at the original event, completed the film a decade after his father's death. It documents hours of conversation and reflection among people who helped make Harlem a center of Black American culture. The film works as both a historical archive and a portrait of a vanished era.

15110.one_liner: Turkish-language drama about a married couple of artists in Ankara whose careers and marriage collapse after an incident at a theatre premiere triggers state blacklisting.
15110.long_desc: Actress Derya and dramaturgy professor Aziz are respected artists in Ankara until an incident at a play's premiere provokes state reprisals, costing them their jobs, income and home and forcing a move to Istanbul. As they slide into poverty, Aziz holds onto his principles while Derya turns pragmatic, straining their marriage. Directed by İlker Çatak (The Teachers' Lounge), the film draws on real Turkish practices of blacklisting government critics. It won the Golden Bear for Best Film at Berlinale 2026. Runtime 128 minutes.

15228.one_liner: Colombian crime drama about a young immigrant vineyard worker sent to steal an emerald from a church near Medellín, which drifts away from a straight heist plot into loose, sensory filmmaking.
15228.long_desc: Machado, a young Colombian working in French vineyards, is assigned to steal a valuable emerald from a church near Medellín. What starts as a heist setup loosens into an impressionistic, drifting film more interested in tropical landscapes, color and movement than plot mechanics. It is the feature debut of director Simón Vélez, based partly on events from the lead actor's own life, and premiered in Berlinale's Forum section. Spanish/French dialogue, 70 minutes.

15315.one_liner: Polish mockumentary-style fiction film reimagining the life of conceptual artist Oskar Dawicki as a plotted "artist biography," using performance art in place of painting.
15315.long_desc: A hybrid fiction/documentary following artist Oskar Dawicki through a constructed storyline populated by art-world stock characters - the romantic artist, the collector, the gallerist, a rival colleague. Directors Łukasz Ronduda and Maciej Sobieszczański treat performance art, rather than painting, as Dawicki's medium, structuring the film like a gallery exhibition told as a plot. It won the THINK:FILM Award at Berlinale 2015. English subtitles; the festival notes content warnings for sensitive material. 62 minutes, Poland, 2015.

15139.one_liner: French-Polish drama about two long-haul truck drivers, Étienne and Bartosz, who fall for each other and try to sustain a relationship across borders and shifts.
15139.long_desc: Étienne is a French truck driver whose life is warehouses, border crossings and rest stops; his routine changes when he meets Polish driver Bartosz, whose optimism contrasts with his own resignation. As working conditions worsen, the two struggle to keep their relationship going in stolen moments between jobs. It is director Pierre Le Gall's feature debut, presented at Cannes Critics' Week 2026. Romance/drama, 90 minutes, France/Poland co-production.

15198.one_liner: Portuguese comedy-drama about a Lisbon film-industry underdog - an unemployed screenwriter and a junior production assistant - navigating precarious jobs and a possible romance.
15198.long_desc: João, an out-of-work screenwriter, and Clary, a junior production assistant, navigate Lisbon's film industry, marked by low pay, few prospects and burnt-out colleagues. The film is both an insider satire of industry frustration and a romantic, cinephile-minded story about chance encounters and film love. It is director Pedro Ramalhete's feature debut. Comedy-drama, 71 minutes, Portugal, 2025.

15066.one_liner: Spanish experimental essay film in which a filmmaker restores lost reels shot by an obscure amateur director who died mysteriously decades earlier, told entirely without dialogue.
15066.long_desc: An unnamed filmmaker restores rediscovered footage shot by Gérard Fleury, an amateur director who died under mysterious circumstances decades before. Rather than solving the mystery, José Luis Guerín's 1997 film foregrounds visual texture, composition and the unreliability of memory, blurring documentary and fiction with no dialogue at all. It won prizes at the Sitges and Fantasporto festivals in 1997. Note: this screening pairs the feature with the short film "Płomień" (Flame, 2018) by Sami van Ingen.

15160.one_liner: Hungarian autobiographical drama, first part of Márta Mészáros's trilogy, about a teenage girl returning from the USSR in 1946 to be raised by a state security officer after her parents were killed under Stalin.
15160.long_desc: In 1946, teenage Juli returns to Hungary from the Soviet Union; both her parents died during Stalin's purges. She is adopted by a family friend who now works as a Hungarian state security officer, who gives her material comfort but faces Juli's resentment and rebellion, including skipping school to go to the cinema. The film is the first installment of director Márta Mészáros's autobiographical trilogy, starring Zsuzsa Czinkóczi. It won the Grand Prize at Cannes 1984. Hungary, 1984, drama.

15354.tytulOrg: Le journal d'une femme de chambre
15354.one_liner: Romanian director Radu Jude's dark comedy-satire updating Octave Mirbeau's "Diary of a Chambermaid," about a Romanian migrant maid in Paris who stages amateur theatrical versions of the novel for her wealthy employers.
15354.long_desc: Gianina, a Romanian migrant worker in contemporary Paris, works as a maid for a wealthy, pseudo-intellectual couple and by night performs amateur reenactments of Octave Mirbeau's classic novel for their entertainment, while staying in touch with her daughter who lives abroad. Director Radu Jude uses the century-old source material (previously filmed by Renoir and Buñuel) to build a satire of modern servitude and exploitation, described as darkly comic yet "surprisingly tender." Romania/France, 2026, 94 minutes.

15138.one_liner: Austrian documentary in which director Jola Wieczorek traces her family's late-1980s emigration from Poland to Austria through letters, home footage and archival material.
15138.long_desc: Using letters, personal recollections, archival footage and home movies, director Jola Wieczorek (in her feature documentary debut) reconstructs her parents' emigration from a Poznań apartment to Austria in the late 1980s. The film widens from personal family history into a broader portrait of Eastern European families seeking opportunity in the West, gaining added weight during production when Wieczorek's mother's health began declining. It won the Max Ophüls Prize for Best Documentary and a Local Artist Award at Crossing Europe 2026. Austria, 81 minutes.

15135.one_liner: Horror-tinged period drama set in a small Wisconsin town after the Civil War, where a sheriff-pastor fights a diphtheria outbreak that kills his own child.
15135.long_desc: Sheriff and pastor Jacob Hansen investigates a vagrant's death in the woods near his small post-Civil War Wisconsin town; a doctor rules it diphtheria, and the disease then spreads through the community, killing multiple residents including Hansen's own child. Adapted from Stewart O'Nan's 1999 novel, the film mixes horror, western and psychological drama, playing more like a grim morality tale than a conventional western. It is director Dara Van Dusen's feature debut. Norway/Greece/UK/Sweden co-production, 95 minutes.

15243.one_liner: Experimental sci-fi/essay film about a Columbia University researcher investigating the "chronovisor," a device a 1950s Vatican-linked monk allegedly built to view the past.
15243.long_desc: Dr. Béatrice Courte, a Columbia University researcher, investigates the legend of the "chronovisor," a device supposedly invented in the 1950s by Benedictine monk and physicist Pellegrino Ernetti to watch historical events unfold. Through archival research and interviews with people worldwide who may have knowledge of the device, the film blends real and speculative material, citing Borges and Eco as influences. Shot on 16mm, it premiered at Rotterdam 2026. USA, 99 minutes, experimental/speculative fiction.

15080.one_liner: Argentine psychological drama about a fashion designer who secretly survives jumping into an icy river, then unravels physically and mentally back home.
15080.long_desc: Lina, an aspiring fashion designer, impulsively jumps from a bridge into an icy river during a work trip abroad and survives. Back in Buenos Aires she tells no one, but develops a paralyzing fear of water and a growing sense that she never fully returned - alongside physical symptoms like a skin rash and lank hair. Shot with minimalist, film-noir-inspired visuals, it's a slow psychological unraveling rather than a plot-driven thriller. Won the RTVE-Otra Mirada Award at San Sebastian 2025; also played Toronto and New York.

15364.one_liner: French metaphysical thriller in which a woman's consciousness transfers into a man's body after they sleep together, unraveling both their identities.
15364.long_desc: Introverted photographer David meets a mysterious woman, Eva, at a party; after they have sex, Eva finds her mind has somehow moved into David's body. The two spiral into an increasingly surreal reality where memory, identity, and physical form no longer hold together. Based on the graphic novel 'The Case of David Zimmerman', with Lea Seydoux and Niels Schneider leading and director Radu Jude in a cameo. Won in the main competition at Cannes; contains strobe lighting effects.

15250.one_liner: American tragicomedy about a Brooklyn artist who rents out her spare room to a revolving cast of difficult roommates to afford the city.
15250.long_desc: Marie is an artist in a small, gentrifying Brooklyn apartment who takes in one roommate after another to make rent. Each new tenant, initially harmless-seeming, becomes a source of friction, forcing Marie to confront her own patience, anxieties, and ideas about self-sufficiency. It's a bittersweet comedy about housing precarity and forced intimacy with strangers, and the directorial debut of Maria Petschnig, who drew on her own experience of 60-plus roommates over two decades in New York. Contains trigger-warning content per the festival listing.

15188.one_liner: 1990 Polish semi-documentary following children with intellectual disabilities at a care facility as they take music lessons with a new instructor.
15188.long_desc: Set in a residential care center in Kozice Dolne, the film follows children participating in music classes with a new teacher, using a loosely scripted scenario while the participants' emotional reactions - joy, frustration, anger, sorrow - are genuine and unscripted. Directed by Jacek Blawut, it was considered groundbreaking for its time in how it portrayed intellectually disabled subjects as young people with their own desires rather than as objects of pity. Won the Journalists' Award at Gdynia 1990 and the FIPRESCI Prize at Mannheim-Heidelberg 1991. The festival notes the film may raise present-day concerns about privacy given its child subjects.

15395.kraj: Wenezuela, Włochy, Kanada, Luksemburg, Hiszpania, Meksyk
15395.one_liner: Venezuelan gothic thriller starring Asia Argento as a woman who returns after 20 years abroad to sell her family's decaying cocoa plantation, only to find it occupied by workers' families.
15395.long_desc: Caro comes back to Venezuela after two decades away to sell an inherited cocoa estate, but finds the crumbling property still inhabited by former plantation workers and their families, who depend on it for shelter. Her push to reclaim the land escalates into violent conflict over ownership, memory, and power, surfacing the estate's colonial history. The film blends psychological thriller with 'tropical gothic' and Italian giallo influences. Contains strobe lighting effects; director Jorge Thielen Armand is a 2021 Guggenheim Fellow.

15143.one_liner: Austrian semi-documentary about an aging Vienna blues musician who dreams of the Mississippi Delta while facing eviction from his soon-to-be-demolished building.
15143.long_desc: Alois Koch, who goes by 'Al Cook', is a melancholic blues musician living near the Danube in Vienna, a city he finds provincial compared to the Mississippi Delta blues scene he idolizes. As the last remaining resident of a building slated for demolition, he holds a yard sale of his possessions, which becomes an occasion to encounter Vienna's other eccentric characters. The film mixes documentary observation with staged elements and blends melancholy with dry humor. Directors Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel previously won awards including one for 'Vera' (Venice 2022).

15029.one_liner: Documentary-fiction hybrid set in Minsk about a model and a morgue restorer who play fictionalized versions of themselves as they form a cautious relationship amid Belarus's political unrest.
15029.long_desc: Masza, training at modeling school for an international career while hiding inner sadness, and Mikhail, who does restorative cosmetic work in a morgue and paints dark imagery in private, are real people playing themselves in this staged-documentary experiment. Their tentative connection develops through summer walks in Minsk as Belarus's political tensions rise in the background; only their meeting was arranged for the camera, marking both subjects' film debut. Winner of the Special Jury Prize and Best Performance at Locarno 2025, Best Film at Sarajevo 2025, and other awards. Content warnings noted by the festival.

15374.one_liner: Drama transposing Virginia Woolf's Mrs Dalloway to present-day Lagos, following one day in the life of an elite Nigerian woman preparing an evening party.
15374.long_desc: The film follows a single day in the life of a wealthy Lagos woman as she prepares to host a gathering, encountering people from her past and present who prompt reflection on her life choices, lost loves, and missed chances. A parallel storyline follows a soldier suffering PTSD from fighting Boko Haram, contrasting the protagonist's privileged world with Nigeria's harsher realities. Directed by Arie and Chuko Esiri (previously behind 'Eyimofe'), it stars Sophie Okonedo, Ayo Edebiri, and David Oyelowo, and premiered in the Quinzaine des cineastes at Cannes.

15152.one_liner: Lithuanian drama about a 30-year-old man who returns to his late father's seaside childhood home to sell it, and instead drifts into an unplanned vacation confronting grief and impending fatherhood.
15152.long_desc: Danielius comes back to his childhood home by the sea intending to sell it after his father's death, but his practical errand dissolves into an aimless stay in a place that's now familiar yet foreign to him. The film wanders through his grief, his anxiety about becoming a father himself, and nostalgia for a lost sense of security, as he says a quiet goodbye to his youth. Co-written by Maria Kavtaradze and edited by Laurynas Bareisa, it won Best Director in the main competition at Karlovy Vary 2025.

15208.one_liner: Sami-language musical drama set in Norway's Sapmi region about siblings caught between fighting a mining company and confronting buried family trauma.
15208.long_desc: Siblings Maia and Danel face a crisis in their reindeer-herding community as mining interests threaten their land. Maia brings their uncle Lemme back from Canada, a man who once successfully halted a mining project on Sami territory, but his return dredges up old family trauma, worsening Danel's struggles with alcohol. Incorporating traditional joik singing and Sami spiritual ritual, the film weighs individual versus community and tradition versus industry against stunning Nordic landscapes. It's the debut feature by choreographer-filmmaker Elle Sofe Sara and premiered in Berlinale's Panorama section; contains content warnings.

15103.one_liner: Polish drama about two young Warsaw artists from different class backgrounds falling into their first serious adult relationship, which reopens old emotional wounds.
15103.long_desc: Maria, from a wealthy Warsaw family, and Patryk, a struggling art student, fall into a relationship that becomes a mirror for their respective pasts and insecurities, complicated by their differing socioeconomic backgrounds. The film engages with Generation Z anxieties around intimacy and 'new masculinity' open to vulnerability, and the therapeutic role art can play in relationships. Directed by Lukasz Ronduda and inspired by real-life artists Patryk Rozycki and Karolina Balcer, plus the art project 'Skup lez'. Premiered in the Big Screen Competition at Rotterdam; contains content/trigger warnings.

15124.one_liner: Experimental opera-film in which a depressed Paris-based rapper becomes convinced he is Mozart, intercut with the real Mozart's 1778 crisis in Paris.
15124.long_desc: A rapper in contemporary Paris, struggling with depression, aimlessness, substance use, and creative block, develops the delusion that he is Mozart, and the film draws parallels to Mozart's own breakdown in Paris in 1778 (when, aged 22, he lost his mother). Told through arias and dreamlike, surreal visuals blending video art and performance, it's described as simultaneously intimate and absurd. Directed by Iranian audiovisual artist Filmsaaz (b. 1999), whose work has shown at Cannes, Berlin, Venice, and Locarno. Contains strobing lights.

15091.tytulPl: Jeśli się przewrócę, nie podnoś mnie
15091.tytulEn: If I Fall, Don’t Pick Me Up
15091.tytulOrg: If I Fall, Don’t Pick Me Up
15091.one_liner: Irish experimental essay film reconstructing 1974 Berlin, where theatre director Walter Asmus helped Samuel Beckett stage his first self-directed 'Waiting for Godot'.
15091.long_desc: The film documents Berlin in 1974 through the real relationship between Walter Asmus and playwright Samuel Beckett, who worked together on Beckett's first self-directed production of 'Waiting for Godot' and became lifelong friends. Director Declan Clarke interweaves footage of Berlin locations Beckett frequented with archival and textual material, using the city's empty, modernist spaces as an emotional guide to the story. It's a slow, museum-essay-film style work rather than a conventional narrative. Won a Special Recognition in the international competition at FIDMarseille 2024. Screens paired with the short 'Gdzie się podziali wszyscy moi kochankowie?' (Jean-Claude Rousseau, 2024).

15274.kraj: Norwegia, Niemcy, Dania, Francja, Szwecja, Wielka Brytania, Turcja
15274.one_liner: Norwegian drama about two sisters reuniting with their estranged filmmaker father, who casts a Hollywood star instead of one of them in his comeback film.
15274.long_desc: Sisters Nora and Agnes reconnect with their estranged father Gustav, a once-celebrated film director attempting a comeback after years away. When Gustav offers the lead role in his new film to Nora and she turns it down, he instead casts American star Elle Fanning, upending the family's fragile dynamics. Directed by Joachim Trier (The Worst Person in the World), starring Renate Reinsve and Stellan Skarsgård. Won the Grand Prix at Cannes 2025 and Best International Feature at the 2026 Oscars and BAFTA. A family drama about art, ambition, and reconciliation.

15283.tytulEn: By the River That Isn't There
15283.one_liner: 1991 Polish coming-of-age drama about four teenage boys in a small provincial town whose friendship is tested when a girl moves in one summer.
15283.long_desc: Set in a small Polish town in the 1960s, the film follows four teenage boys nicknamed Admirał, Ataman, Wódz and Pasza as they drink cheap wine and kill time over a boring summer. Their group dynamic shifts when an attractive newcomer, Marta, arrives, introducing them to romantic rivalry and heartbreak. Adapted from a short story by Stanisław Czycz and directed by Andrzej Barański, who called it a personal, nostalgic look back at his own youth. Screens as part of the festival's outdoor programme at Zamek w Leśnicy.

15353.one_liner: Chilean mystery/coming-of-age drama set in 1992, where a nine-year-old girl at her grandparents' Andes ski hotel befriends a young athlete who then vanishes.
15353.long_desc: Chile, 1992: nine-year-old Inés spends her holidays at her grandparents' hotel near a ski resort in the Andes, where she befriends Hanna, a German skier training with the Olympic team under a demanding coach. When Hanna mysteriously disappears, Inés's fascination turns into unease as the search uncovers secrets hidden within the hotel and within a country still grappling with its dictatorial past. Directed by Manuela Martelli (Chile '76), pairing a child's-eye mystery with a meditation on Chile's suppressed historical memory. Slow-paced, understated tone; screening in the festival's International Competition.

15355.one_liner: Spanish drama spanning 1932, 1937 and 2017 that traces three gay men's lives across generations, built around an unfinished text by Federico García Lorca.
15355.long_desc: Directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (Skins, Smiley, The Prince) weave historical fact and myth around poet Federico García Lorca into a story about three men across three time periods: 1932, 1937 and 2017. It centers on a wealthy, closeted man seeking membership in a casino who is rejected by a homophobic committee via secret ballot -- white balls mean acceptance, black balls mean rejection, giving the film its title. The film explores desire, repression, shame and Catholic guilt, framed as connecting generations of gay men whose stories were erased by violence or silence. Runtime 155 minutes, Spain/France 2026, screening as a Gala show.

15235.one_liner: Vampire comedy where Isabelle Huppert plays a resurrected Elizabeth Báthory stalking modern Vienna in latex and glitter with her maid, hunting a life-giving elixir.
15235.long_desc: Loosely based on the legend of 16th-century Hungarian countess and alleged serial killer Elizabeth Báthory, the film follows the resurrected countess (Isabelle Huppert) and her maid (Birgit Minichmayr) through contemporary Vienna as they search for a "red elixir of life" and a hidden family history tied to a book that could end their vampire lineage. Directed by veteran experimental filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger, co-written with Nobel laureate Elfriede Jelinek (The Piano Teacher). Campy, deliberately artificial tone mixing dark humor, kitsch and Austro-Hungarian mythology, with bumbling vampire hunters (including performer Conchita Wurst) in pursuit. Premiered at Berlinale 2026; part of the festival's "Mistrzynie, Mistrzowie" retrospective sidebar.

15212.one_liner: Derek Jarman's 1990 experimental film-diary shot around his cottage garden on the English coast, made after his HIV diagnosis, with no conventional plot.
15212.long_desc: A deeply personal, non-narrative work by British director Derek Jarman, made at Prospect Cottage on the Dungeness coast -- the garden he cultivated after being diagnosed with HIV. Rather than tell a story, the film assembles a kaleidoscope of surreal 16mm/35mm images -- wind-blown flowers, grass, waves and clotheslines -- interwoven with diary-like reflections later published as the book Modern Nature. It functions as a meditation on mortality and a critique of conservative Britain in the late 1980s/early 90s, with the garden as a symbol of paradise and refuge. Won an award at Berlinale 1991. Screens paired with the short "Piękne kwiaty i ich hodowla" (Beautiful Flowers and How to Grow Them) by Sarah Wood, as part of the "Garden Party" strand.

15238.kraj: Indonezja, Singapur, Filipiny, Francja, Tajwan, Tajlandia, Korea Południowa
15238.one_liner: Indonesian drama about a young man training to become a shaman who leads trance-possession parties, trying to raise money to stop his family losing their home.
15238.long_desc: In an Indonesian town where communal ecstasy comes through spirit possession, Bayu aspires to become the shaman of a trance party -- inducing collective trance through music and ritual -- to raise money and prevent his family's eviction, while his father plans to sell their home and move to the capital. Along the way he is helped by, and drawn closer to, Laksmi and the singer Asri. Directed by Wregas Bhanuteja, the film blends real and invented Indonesian ritual and dance traditions with themes of community, tradition versus capitalist pressure, and self-discovery. Premiered at Sundance 2026; screens in the festival's late-night "Nocne Szaleństwo" strand.

15090.one_liner: An experimental essay film shot in Paris's Belleville, Ménilmontant and La Roquette neighborhoods during the COVID-19 pandemic, observing everyday life among African and Middle Eastern diaspora communities through taxi rides, street scenes, and a young woman alone in her apartment.
15090.long_desc: Site-specific poetic essay film built from three overlapping visual threads: conversations recorded in taxis, footage of street traffic, and scenes of a young woman alone in a small Paris apartment. Shot during COVID-19 lockdown in multicultural eastern Paris districts rarely seen by tourists. Built from repetition, chance encounters and daily routines rather than plot, evoking Marguerite Duras and Chantal Akerman. Won an award at FIDMarseille. Screens paired with the short film 'Miłość na ścieżce jeżyn' (Love on the Bramble Path, dir. Sophie Roger, France, 2025, 24 min).

15202.kraj: Singapur, Wielka Brytania, Filipiny, Francja, Holandia
15202.one_liner: A drama set at a luxury tropical resort in the Philippines that follows the invisible service staff who maintain the illusion of paradise for wealthy guests.
15202.long_desc: Set inside a manicured luxury resort, the film examines the hidden labor - housekeeping, groundskeeping, service with a smile - that sustains an image of paradise for guests. Rather than overt conflict, tension builds through small cracks in the performance: a smile held too long, a worker briefly breaking character. Director Rafael Manuel favors quiet observation and social critique over spectacle, using the resort as a metaphor for class and labor inequality. Screens paired with the short film 'She Dolls with Dolly' (dir. Karin Fisslthaler, Austria, 2024, 3 min).

15305.one_liner: A 1982 Colombian horror-satire in which a wealthy, terminally ill plantation owner is kept alive by regular blood transfusions while young men mysteriously vanish from the city.
15305.long_desc: A rich, dying sugar-plantation patriarch depends on constant blood transfusions to survive; his family's aides resort to abducting and killing young people to supply blood, while the city panics over disappearances blamed on 'the Monster of Mangones.' Loosely based on real events - the murder of dozens of street children in Cali, Colombia, in the 1960s-70s. Director Luis Ospina mixes vampire-horror tropes with black comedy and crime-thriller elements to satirize class privilege and elite indifference. A key work of Colombian 'tropical gothic' cinema, screening in the festival's Tropikalny Gotyk section.

15295.one_liner: A drama in which 17-year-old Marina travels to Vigo, Spain to obtain paperwork needed for a university scholarship, and in doing so uncovers a long-hidden family secret.
15295.long_desc: Marina returns to her father's hometown of Vigo to get a document required for a scholarship application, and the visit forces her extended family to confront a secret they've suppressed for years. Director Carla Simón (Alcarràs) blends present-day scenes with home-movie/archival-style footage to explore family memory, shame, and denial. The story doubles as a tribute to relatives lost to the AIDS epidemic whose deaths were erased or hidden within family history. A personal, semi-autobiographical drama about uncovering one's roots.

15239.one_liner: A post-apocalyptic genre film set in a fuel-refinery city-state ruled by a cult of macho masculinity, where women are traded for gasoline until a female uprising challenges the male leader's chosen successor.
15239.long_desc: In a post-apocalyptic city built around a giant refinery, men trade fuel for women and food while worshipping their leader, Nikos. Maria, a tough woman positioned to become his successor, has her plans upended when the mysterious, liberated Eleni arrives and pushes her toward rebellion. The film mixes kitsch aesthetics, neon-lit cinematography and classical/mythic references to stage a clash between toxic masculinity and a militant, queer-inflected matriarchy. A genre mashup of sci-fi, feminist allegory, and erotic thriller.

15229.one_liner: A documentary about jaripeo (Mexican bull-riding rodeo culture) that follows Noé, a traditional cowboy, and Joseph, a gender-nonconforming participant, inside this hypermasculine world.
15229.long_desc: Documentary look at jaripeo, the Mexican bull-riding tradition rooted in cattle-ranching culture, the regional counterpart to the American rodeo. It centers on two figures within the scene: Noé, a conventional cowboy, and Joseph, who doesn't fit the binary gender norms typical of the milieu, as both navigate attraction, family pressures, and self-discovery. Shot on Super 8 combined with music-video-style visuals, mixing communal rodeo scenes with intimate personal conversation. Explores queerness and identity inside a traditionally hypermasculine subculture.

15294.one_liner: A survival-thriller drama in which a father (Sergi López), accompanied by his young son, searches for his missing daughter through illegal desert rave parties in Morocco.
15294.long_desc: A father scours illegal, off-grid rave parties in the Moroccan desert looking for his missing daughter. After days of searching he falls in with a group of itinerant ravers and travels with them toward the Mauritanian border, where the journey turns dangerous and events spiral out of control. Won the Jury Prize at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival. Combines road-movie and survival-thriller elements against a backdrop of rave culture and social/political breakdown; described as an increasingly intense, unpredictable ride.

15240.one_liner: A drama about two teenage boys, Naim and Ryan, whose intense romantic relationship in a religious, industrial-town setting turns fatal after they are subjected to conversion therapy.
15240.long_desc: Naim, a new student, moves with his religiously fundamentalist mother to an industrial town, where he becomes involved with Ryan, a rougher classmate. Their immediate, intense connection develops into a relationship their community rejects, and the boys are subjected to conversion therapy with fatal consequences. The title references the Book of Leviticus, a biblical text some interpret as condemning homosexuality. Framed as a cautionary tale about religious extremism and attempts to suppress identity through faith-based 'conversion' practices.

15352.one_liner: A drama in which a mother and her surviving daughter, still grieving a year after a party ended in tragedy, are drawn back together with the dead girl's boyfriend during a family holiday in Tenerife.
15352.long_desc: Teenager Jessie attends a party with her boyfriend Lux the night before a planned family holiday, and the evening ends in tragedy. A year later her mother Ella and younger sister are still moving through daily life on autopilot when Lux reappears, stirring unspoken blame and a desperate need for forgiveness. Ella impulsively invites him along on the family's previously cancelled trip to Tenerife, where the three try to survive each other's grief under the Spanish sun. The film won the Grand Prize in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes 2026. Directed by Sandra Wollner (Germany/Austria, 2026, 121 min, German dialogue).

15310.one_liner: A psychological thriller about a high-powered corporate consultant whose tightly controlled life unravels as she hides an affair with her boss and her sister's mental illness.
15310.long_desc: Lola is an elite management consultant who maintains a facade of perfection while secretly involved with her boss and dealing with her sister's psychiatric crisis. She keeps up the performance through minimal sleep and punishing early-morning workouts, but as work pressure mounts, paranoid thoughts start intruding on her daily reality. The film traces her psychological breakdown as her carefully constructed life comes apart. It premiered in competition at the 2019 Berlinale and received seven Austrian Film Award nominations. Directed by Marie Kreutzer (Austria, 2019, 108 min).

15037.one_liner: A fantasy-drama narrated from the point of view of a hen who flees a factory farm with her chicks and gets caught up in theft and revenge in a Greek seaside village.
15037.long_desc: After escaping an industrial poultry farm, a determined hen searches for safety for her chicks and ends up entangled in the affairs of a Greek coastal village, witnessing theft and predatory behavior connected to migration. Told largely from the bird's perspective, the film is described as "an original tale of vengeance" using an animal narrator to examine human cruelty and nature. The eight hens on screen are real, individually named Hungarian chickens. It received a Platform Prize honorable mention at TIFF 2025. Directed by György Pálfi (Germany/Greece/Hungary, 2025, 96 min).

15203.one_liner: A documentary visiting post-industrial sites in Detroit, South Dakota, Zurich and Geneva to profile gardeners and activists who treat growing plants as a form of resistance.
15203.long_desc: This documentary follows nature reclaiming urban decay across Detroit, South Dakota, Zurich and Geneva, profiling the people who tend it. Subjects include Detroit community gardeners, Native American gardener Milo Yellow Hair, gardener Maurice Maggio, and the Geneva cooperative Jardins de Cocagne, for whom cultivation is both daily practice and personal philosophy. The film frames gardening as a deliberate, patient alternative to consumerism rather than a mere hobby. Directed by Nicolas Humbert (Switzerland/Germany, 2016, 108 min), it screens in the festival's "Garden Party" strand.

15182.one_liner: A near-wordless documentary observing the daily prayer, work and silence of Carthusian monks at the Grande Chartreuse monastery in the French Alps.
15182.long_desc: After waiting nearly two decades for the monks' permission, director Philip Gröning spent over six months living inside La Grande Chartreuse to film the Carthusian order's daily routine. The film has almost no dialogue, music or narration, instead observing prayer, manual work and silence as they unfold in real time. It won the Special Jury Prize at Sundance 2006 and Best Documentary at the European Film Awards 2006. Directed by Philip Gröning (Germany/France/Switzerland, 2005, 162 min, French and Latin).

15064.one_liner: A slow-burn drama in which two branches of a wealthy Argentine family idle away a stagnant, decaying summer together at a rural villa.
15064.long_desc: During a humid summer, two related wealthy families occupy a decaying country estate, drifting through fragmented conversations and directionless days. Rather than a single dramatic collapse, the film shows a slow erosion of family bonds and class privilege through neglect, boredom and inertia. This is Lucrecia Martel's debut feature; it won the Alfred Bauer Prize at the 2001 Berlinale and prizes at the Havana and Toulouse Latin American film festivals. Argentina/France/Spain/Japan, 2001, 102 min, Spanish.

15196.one_liner: A shorts program of four films centered on close, character-driven relationships that rework familiar family and folk-tale archetypes.
15196.long_desc: This anthology screens four short films together, including "Macocha" (Stepmother, dir. Adam Porębowicz, Poland 2025, 28 min), described as a modern parable in the style of Hirokazu Koreeda that reworks the fairy-tale stepmother figure, alongside "Mix," "Kołysanka dla psa" (Lullaby for a Dog), and "Princeska" (Princess). The selected shorts share a focus on intimate, personal relationships rather than genre convention, aiming to strip familiar character types of stereotype and prejudice.

15289.one_liner: A drama spanning three time periods (1908, 1972, 2020) whose separate characters are all secretly connected through a single ginkgo tree in a German university botanical garden.
15289.long_desc: Three stories unfold around the same ginkgo tree in a botanical garden: in 1908 a woman named Grete fights to be admitted to botany studies despite gender barriers; in 1972 researcher Gundula runs plant-sensitivity experiments with an assistant; and in 2020 a professor and a botanist investigate the boundary between the visible and invisible natural world. The tree is the only witness to the hidden bonds linking these people across more than a century. The film won the FIPRESCI Prize at Venice 2025 and Best Film at Valladolid 2025. Directed by Ildikó Enyedi (Germany/Hungary/France/China, 2025, 147 min, color and black-and-white).

15142.one_liner: A black-and-white comedy-drama about a solitude-craving woman in Mexico whose quiet routine of sudoku and TV is upended when she reluctantly takes in a lodger.
15142.long_desc: Olga wants nothing more than to be left alone with her sudoku puzzles and television, but a buzzing fly, noisy neighbors, a broken elevator, health troubles and money problems keep intruding on her peace. When she reluctantly rents a spare room to a man visiting his hospitalized wife nearby, her fragile solitude unravels further. The film mixes neorealism with slapstick comedy in a Chaplin-esque register, centering compassion among people living on the margins. It is director Fernando Eimbcke's fifth feature. Mexico, 2026, 102 min, black and white, Spanish.

15112.one_liner: A black-and-white period drama set in 17th-century Protestant Germany about a woman posing as a male war veteran who is gradually absorbed into an isolated village.
15112.long_desc: A woman disguised as a man arrives in an isolated German farming village claiming to be heir to an abandoned farm. Through forged documents and diligent work she wins the community's trust and is drawn deep into its rigid social order, but the more embedded she becomes, the more her invented identity threatens to crack. The film stars Sandra Hüller, who won Best Supporting Actress at Berlinale 2026; it also won Best Screenplay at the Istanbul Film Festival and at Diagonale 2026. Directed by Markus Schleinzer (Austria/Germany, 2026, 93 min, black and white, German).

15377.kraj: Singapur, Francja, Norwegia, Chiny, Hongkong, Indonezja, Katar, Tajlandia
15377.one_liner: A family dramedy following a multigenerational Thai family on a one-day pilgrimage to nine temples to secure their dying grandmother's place in heaven.
15377.long_desc: After a fortune teller predicts that an elderly matriarch won't live to see her next birthday, her extended family takes her on a single-day pilgrimage to nine temples to secure her passage to heaven. The reluctant, exhausting journey turns into a mix of comedic misunderstandings and intergenerational confrontations and confessions. Along the way the film contrasts ancient ritual with mundane modern life, including monks navigating present-day technology. It premiered in the Directors' Fortnight at Cannes; director Sompot Chidgasornpongse spent two decades as an assistant to Apichatpong Weerasethakul. Thailand/Singapore/France/Norway/China/Hong Kong/Indonesia/Qatar, 2026, 140 min.

15326.one_liner: A surrealist blend of ethnographic documentary and fiction about a European woman traveling the Trans-Siberian railway who is captured and taken into the Mongolian steppe.
15326.long_desc: Lady Windemere and her fellow passengers are riding the Trans-Siberian railway when they are seized and brought into the Mongolian steppes, where their encounters with nomadic life transform their identities and worldviews. The film blends ethnographic documentary technique with surrealist fiction to explore East-West cultural collision and mythmaking. It won Best Visual Design at the German Film Awards 1989, the Audience Prize at the Montreal International Festival of New Cinema, and was named Film of the Year at the London Film Festival. Directed by Ulrike Ottinger (Germany, 1989, 166 min).

15360.one_liner: Pedro Almodóvar's drama interweaves two stories of filmmakers battling creative block, one set during his own 2004 production of Bad Education.
15360.long_desc: The film follows Raúl, an accomplished director stuck in a creative crisis while making a film in 2004, and Elsa, a former arthouse director turned advertising professional who returns to filmmaking despite debilitating migraines. Both draw material from the misfortunes of people around them: Elsa from her friends, Raúl from his assistant and partner. Structured as two interlocking films, it is Almodóvar's reflection, at age 76, on how artists borrow and steal from real life and eventually hit creative walls. Cast includes Bárbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia and Aitana Sánchez-Gijón; runtime 111 minutes.

15211.kraj: Serbia, Chorwacja, Holandia, Bośnia i Hercegowina
15211.one_liner: An experimental Balkan film follows an insomniac man through nighttime Belgrade into a hidden garden world and an esoteric forest commune blurring the line between the living and the dead.
15211.long_desc: Serbian-Croatian-Dutch-Bosnian experimental feature by Dane Komljen. It opens with an insomniac man wandering Belgrade's rigid, geometric architecture at night before he discovers a hidden, overgrown park where fleeting encounters take place. This leads into a more psychedelic journey to an esoteric commune hidden in dense forest, where the forest floor is treated as a living organism merging with human bodies. The film is deliberately associative and non-narrative, using ambiguous imagery to explore transience, and the garden/forest as a liminal space between paradise, purgatory, and an alternate reality. Runtime 107 minutes; dialogue in Serbian, Slovenian and Arabic.

15145.one_liner: A documentary-fiction hybrid follows a Senegalese-French family across a father's funeral in Guinea-Bissau and a daughter's wedding in France, exploring diaspora, memory and women's role in holding communities together.
15145.long_desc: Directed by Alain Gomis (France/Senegal/Guinea-Bissau), the film moves between two family events on opposite continents - a funeral and a wedding - to portray a scattered community and its migrating memory. It blurs documentary and fiction as it follows family members dealing with trauma, success, failure and the feeling of not fully belonging anywhere after leaving home. The film emphasizes the resilience of women, who despite being undervalued hold the community together and secure its future. It premiered in competition at the 2026 Berlinale. Runtime 184 minutes, in French, Wolof, Manjak and Guinea-Bissau Creole.

15153.tytulEn: Patty Is Such a Girly Name
15153.one_liner: A Greek coming-of-age sports drama follows a teenage judo athlete nicknamed Patty as she trains under a demanding coach in Athens and falls for a rival competitor.
15153.long_desc: Directed by Giorgos Georgopoulos, the film follows Daphne ('Patty'), a young judoka who moves from a small island to Athens to train under the strict sensei Yuri, chasing a spot at the Olympics. She faces harsh discipline, personal sacrifice and the temptations of city life, complicated by a romantic connection with Zoe, an athlete from a rival team. The film combines sports drama, teen coming-of-age story and queer romance, portraying the girls' judo community with a documentary-like eye. It won several awards at the 2025 Thessaloniki Film Festival, including Best Greek Film. Runtime 113 minutes.

15028.one_liner: A post-apocalyptic fable follows a nine-year-old girl living in a world without adults, who encounters a prophet figure in a sequence adapted from a Don DeLillo play.
15028.long_desc: Directed by Ben Rivers (UK/France/Canada), the film imagines 'every child's dream' - a world emptied of adults - through nine-year-old Moon, whose freedom is shadowed by displacement and anxiety about the future. It mixes post-apocalyptic imagery with dreamlike, dark fairy-tale elements touching on pandemic and ecological anxieties. A key scene adapts Don DeLillo's 2007 one-act play The Word for Snow, in which Moon meets a mysterious prophet. The film won the Pardo Verde award at Locarno 2025. Runtime 98 minutes, in English and Catalan.

15162.tytulPl: Dziennik dla mojego ojca i matki
15162.tytulEn: Diary for My Father and Mother
15162.one_liner: A 1990 Hungarian drama, the third film in Márta Mészáros's autobiographical trilogy, follows a photographer navigating the aftermath of the crushed 1956 Hungarian uprising.
15162.long_desc: Directed by Márta Mészáros, the film opens with the toppling of Stalin's statue in Budapest during the 1956 revolution and then follows the weeks after Soviet forces suppressed the uprising. Photographer Juli returns from Moscow to Budapest and documents evidence of crimes, moving between her companion in hiding, János, and Magda, a state security official, in a portrait of a distanced, conflicted woman maneuvering between opposing sides. The story climaxes at a chaotic New Year's Eve party reuniting former comrades, with János's fate later echoed in Mészáros's own casting choices. Cast includes Zsuzsa Czinkóczi, Jan Nowicki and Mari Töröcsik. Runtime 116 minutes, in Hungarian and Russian.

15292.one_liner: A German drama interweaves the lives of four generations of women on the same farm between Berlin and Hamburg, spanning both world wars and the postwar division of Germany.
15292.long_desc: Directed by Mascha Schilinski, the film follows Alma in the early 20th century, Erika in the 1940s, Angelika in the 1980s and Lenka in the present day, all connected to the same family farmhouse. Each woman confronts a society that treats women as expendable, marked by male violence and wartime brutality, as time seems to move both forward and backward across the generations. It won the Jury Prize at Cannes 2025 and the Silver Frog at Camerimage, and swept multiple categories including Best Film at the 2026 German Film Awards. Runtime 155 minutes, in German.

15111.one_liner: A US drama follows an eight-year-old girl whose behavior grows disturbing after she witnesses a violent attack in a San Francisco park.
15111.long_desc: Directed by Beth de Araújo, the film follows Josephine, who witnesses a violent assault on a jogger while playing with her father in Golden Gate Park; the attacker is caught, but the trauma changes her. Her parents seek help from psychologists and try to keep her routine stable, but her reactions to the trauma escalate and she seems to mature too fast, straining the family. The film is inspired by traumatic events from the director's own childhood and is her second feature after Soft & Quiet (2022). It won the Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award in the Sundance 2026 American Narrative Competition. Cast includes Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan; runtime 119 minutes.

15244.one_liner: A Mexican-Greek debut feature set at a 1990s Christmas Eve family dinner shows a middle-class Catholic household's holiday facade collapsing into emotional violence.
15244.long_desc: Directed by Racornelia in her feature debut, the film is set during a Christmas Eve dinner in a middle-class Mexican home in the late 1990s, using VHS-inspired visuals to stage the gathering as a kind of theater. Beneath the holiday warmth and Catholic ritual, tension escalates into open emotional explosion, exposing patriarchal power dynamics passed down through family, marriage and religion. Described by the director as blending autobiography and fiction, tenderness and cruelty. The film carries content/trigger warnings for its depiction of family violence. Runtime 118 minutes, in Spanish, English and French.

15207.one_liner: A Norwegian drama follows a suddenly famous young singer who quits touring to deal with depression by taking a quiet teaching job back in her hometown.
15207.long_desc: Directed by Eivind Landsvik in his feature debut, the film follows Maja, a musician whose rapid rise to fame brings on 'great helplessness' and a creative crisis. She steps back from her career, returns home and takes a job at a local school while trying to manage depression and regain control of her life - a process that proves harder than expected. The film draws comparisons to early Joachim Trier for its empathetic take on modern life's pressures. It marks the acting debut of musician Marie Ulven, known as Girl in Red, in the lead role. Runtime 105 minutes, in Norwegian.

15141.one_liner: A Swiss documentary follows two experienced sailors racing across Lake Geneva through shifting weather, shot in a style that shifts from sports film to meditative essay on transience.
15141.long_desc: Directed by Fabrice Aragno in his feature debut, the film follows two sailors competing in a regatta across Lake Geneva, capturing sunny stretches, storms, morning mist and evening light over coastal towns. What begins as a dynamic sports documentary shifts into a contemplative study of the two sailors' relationship, their bond with water, the ever-changing landscape reflected on the lake, and the passage of time. Aragno previously worked as cinematographer for Jean-Luc Godard on films including Film Socialisme and Goodbye to Language. The film won the Ecumenical Jury Special Mention and Young Jury Award at Locarno 2025. Runtime 81 minutes, in French and German.

15189.one_liner: Documentary observing the daily operations of a 1970s New York City welfare office and the people navigating its bureaucracy.
15189.long_desc: A 1975 fly-on-the-wall documentary by Frederick Wiseman set inside a New York City welfare office. It follows caseworkers and the citizens seeking help with housing, unemployment, illness, and family crises as they get tangled in bureaucratic procedure. Shot in black and white with no narration or added drama, the film simply observes interviews and waiting-room encounters as they happen. It won the Cinema Eye Honors Award in 2016 for its enduring relevance.

15082.one_liner: Fiction feature about three women at different stages of life who run an isolated Alpine mountain refuge through the changing seasons.
15082.long_desc: Shot on 16mm and set in a remote alpine hut, the film follows three women in different life stages who each tend the refuge and its guests. For one, isolation is a trap; for another, a necessity; for the third, a chosen peace. Fiction is woven into observational scenes of shifting weather, seasons, local legends, and passing travelers. This is director Manon Coubia's debut feature, which premiered in the Perspectives section at the 2026 Berlinale and won a special jury distinction.

15113.one_liner: Polish drama about a 30-year-old woman who signs up alone for a pole-dance camp after her friend backs out, and starts to reconnect with herself.
15113.long_desc: After her travel companion cancels, 30-year-old Mila attends a pole dance camp by herself, initially eyeing the confident, athletic dancers with irony and distance. Away from her controlling boyfriend and outside her comfort zone, she gradually opens up through training, awkward moments, and late-night talks with the other women. The film is a portrait of a millennial exhausted by unrealistic expectations, centered on themes of self-acceptance and female solidarity. It is a 2026 Polish production distributed by Gutek Film, with audio description available via the Kino Dostępne app.

15233.one_liner: A young nun in an isolated, dying convent has prophetic dreams and is sent on a dangerous desert journey to greet a new archbishop.
15233.long_desc: Rafaela, a nun at a struggling, isolated convent, experiences disturbing visions that may be prophecies. When the community must send someone across the desert to welcome a newly appointed archbishop, she is chosen for the journey. Along the way she encounters other pilgrims, each one reflecting back a piece of the world she is trying to escape. Directed by Karla Badillo (Mexico/Argentina, 2025), the film draws on Buñuel-style irony and dry humor, and its structure and title reference the Spanish board game Juego de la Oca (Game of Geese).

15151.one_liner: Icelandic drama about a volcanologist on a government eruption-safety committee whose professional control clashes with a consuming personal desire.
15151.long_desc: Anna is a volcanologist serving on a committee that manages Iceland's constant volcanic hazards — eruptions, earthquakes, lava flows, and ash. Having inherited from her scientist father a deep sensitivity to the island's harsh nature, she is skilled at containing external threats. The film interweaves this professional world with her private struggle against an overwhelming desire she can't control, using Iceland's raw volcanic landscape as a mirror for the tension between restraint and eruption. Directed by Ugla Hauksdóttir (Iceland, 2025).

15248.one_liner: Coming-of-age drama about a shy teenage boy who helps his father run a home-based amateur porn business and has to find his own idea of intimacy.
15248.long_desc: Alec is a sexually inexperienced teenager whose main education about sex has come from internet pornography — made more complicated by the fact that after school he helps his father shoot amateur adult films at home, where living space and workplace are the same. Rather than focusing on the pornography itself, the film centers on Alec's search for real intimacy amid a household where physical closeness is constantly performed for a camera. Directed by Muriel d'Ansembourg (Netherlands/Belgium/France, 2026), it deals with loneliness, inherited relationship patterns, and the blurred line between recorded experience and authentic connection. The festival page carries multiple content warnings for this title.

15097.one_liner: Wordless black-and-white documentary about people and animals in Iceland living by nature's rhythms among the salvaged wreckage of obsolete technology.
15097.long_desc: Shot with no dialogue in black and white, Carcasse observes human and animal life in Iceland shaped by entropy and the landscape. It imagines a kind of future in which humanity has returned to older, more archaic survival methods, with a new order emerging from collapse. Local communities repurpose obsolete technology in inventive ways, including an abandoned aircraft used as a barn. Directed by Clémentine Roy and Gústav Geir Bollason (France/Iceland, 2017, 60 min), the project also produced a companion book and film installation made with local farmers.

15204.one_liner: Comedy-drama about a Montreal PhD student, stuck on her dissertation and finances, who is nudged by a shaman and a new friend to abandon her carefully planned life.
15204.long_desc: Lucie is a doctoral student in Montreal struggling to finish her dissertation on games in culture while her visa is about to expire and money runs short. Her ex-boyfriend, a struggling actor, resurfaces just as she becomes involved with her thesis advisor. After meeting a mysterious shaman and an energetic new friend named Béatrice in a park, Lucie is pushed to consider walking away from everything she has built. The Canadian film (2026, 148 min) mixes literary and musical references (Dostoevsky, Huizinga, Debussy, Lutosławski) with a light, Rohmer/Rivette/Hong Sang-soo-style tone, and carries a strobing-lights content warning.

15311.one_liner: Costume drama about Empress Elisabeth of Austria ("Sisi") at 40, rebelling against the rigid public image and corseted ideal expected of her.
15311.long_desc: Set in Vienna starting Christmas 1877, the film follows Empress Elisabeth of Bavaria as she turns 40 and faces growing scrutiny of her aging body and famous corseted figure. Rather than accept her ceremonial role, she pushes back, reconnecting with former lovers and staging an elaborate public facade to hide her private defiance. Directed by Marie Kreutzer (Austria/Luxembourg/Germany/France, 2022), the film portrays Elisabeth as an intelligent strategist who manipulates the constraints of her position, presenting the historical figure through a pointedly contemporary, rebellious lens.

15136.one_liner: Feature debut following interconnected stories of ordinary people trapped under siege, including a group hiding in a video rental shop deciding whether to burn their beloved film reels for warmth.
15136.long_desc: Set during a year-long siege, the film weaves together several storylines of civilians facing starvation, sniper fire, explosions, and no medical care, sheltering in basements and ruins. One thread follows film lovers hiding out in a video rental shop who must decide whether to burn their collection of movies to stay warm. Clocks in the film stay frozen around 7:30, evoking a sense of suspended time. Director Abdallah Al-Khatib drew on his own experience under fire during the siege of the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp in Damascus during the Syrian civil war; the film (Algeria/France/Palestine, 2026) won the Best Debut award in the Perspectives section at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival.

15249.one_liner: Swedish documentary-essay/poetic hybrid film about trauma, transgender experience, and the body's fight-flight-freeze survival responses.
15249.long_desc: Artist Ester Bergsmark examines the physiological "fight, flight, and freeze" responses to danger, focusing on freezing as a means of surviving withdrawal and trauma. The film asks how a person returns to life after a long period of shutting down, and whether art can break through that paralysis. Blending documentary essay, poetic imagery, and fairy-tale elements, it draws on Bergsmark's own experience of the hostility faced daily as a transgender person, using images of animals feigning death and other survival strategies in nature as recurring motifs. The Sweden/Norway production (2026, 90 min) premiered at CPH:DOX and carries a strobing-lights warning.

15168.one_liner: A British-Irish drama about a shy young man who is drawn into a leather-clad biker's BDSM relationship, transforming his sheltered life.
15168.long_desc: Colin, a quiet, sheltered young man, is given a number by an assured biker named Ray and begins meeting him whenever summoned. As their relationship deepens into a submissive/dominant dynamic, Colin undergoes a dramatic personal and sexual awakening that unsettles his conventional parents. The film is a 2025 UK/Ireland co-production directed by Harry Lighton, starring Alexander Skarsgård and Harry Melling. It won Best Screenplay and the Palm Dog award in Un Certain Regard at Cannes 2025, and Best Film at the British Independent Film Awards.

15119.one_liner: A minimalist Spanish-language drama set almost entirely in one room, where female composers, a journalist and a famous male artist debate whether real art can be made from everyday noise.
15119.long_desc: Confined largely to one interior space, the film follows three female composers, a TV journalist and a prominent male artist as they talk on and off camera against a backdrop of ambient neighborhood sound. Their conversations circle a single question: does great art require total isolation, or can it be made from the domestic and street noise that women, in particular, transform into music. Directed by Nicolás Pereda (Germany/Canada/Mexico, 2026), the film screened in the Forum section at the 2025 Berlinale and relies on dry, sharp dialogue rather than conventional plot.

15130.one_liner: A Spanish-French road-trip drama in which a difficult elderly father talks his adult son into driving him nearly 24 hours across two countries to see his estranged daughter.
15130.long_desc: An aging, conflicted father persuades his son to drive him from southern Spain to northern France to visit the son's sister, and the nearly day-long car journey becomes a slow-burn study of a strained father-son relationship. Little backstory is spelled out; old tensions surface mostly through what is left unsaid rather than explained. The cast, including Lionel Corral Bernal and Lionel Corral, plays loosely fictionalized versions of themselves with room for improvisation. It is the feature directorial debut of Carlos Saiz Espín and won a special distinction at Valladolid 2025 and the Forward Future Award plus Best Actor at Beijing IFF 2025.

15275.one_liner: Agnieszka Holland's 1993 adaptation of the classic novel, about an orphaned girl who discovers a locked garden and a hidden sickly cousin on her uncle's isolated English estate.
15275.long_desc: In 1901, ten-year-old Mary returns to England from India after her parents' deaths and is sent to live at her uncle's remote, gloomy manor house. She finds the key to a walled garden that has stood locked for years and, with the help of a local boy named Dickon, begins secretly restoring it. In the process she discovers her cousin Colin, a sickly boy long confined to his room, and helps draw him back into life. Directed by Agnieszka Holland, with cinematography by Roger Deakins and a score by Zbigniew Preisner, this US/UK production was made with Francis Ford Coppola's backing and is screened here as a classic revival.

15284.one_liner: Peter Weir's 1975 Australian mystery-drama about schoolgirls from a strict Victorian boarding school who vanish during a Valentine's Day picnic at a remote rock formation.
15284.long_desc: On Valentine's Day 1900, students from an exclusive girls' boarding school take an outing into the Australian bush, where several of them disappear without explanation at Hanging Rock. The disappearance and its unresolved aftermath expose the rigid social order of the school and colonial society. Based on Joan Lindsay's novel, the film is considered a landmark of the Australian New Wave and won a BAFTA for Best Cinematography. It is presented here as a classic revival screening.

15262.one_liner: Samuel Fuller's 1964 black-and-white film noir about a former sex worker who tries to start over in a small town and uncovers the abuses hidden behind its respectable facade.
15262.long_desc: A woman leaves sex work behind and settles in a seemingly wholesome small American town, taking a job caring for disabled children. As she is drawn into the community, she discovers that its most respected citizens harbor darker secrets and abuses of power than anything in her past. Directed by Samuel Fuller, the film is known for a provocative opening scene and blunt social critique, and influenced the French New Wave. Shot in black and white, 90 minutes, screened here as part of a classics/repertory selection.

15328.one_liner: Ulrike Ottinger's 2007 documentary about Vienna's historic Prater amusement park, tracing its shift from imperial hunting grounds to a mass-entertainment fairground.
15328.long_desc: Through archival footage and observational filming, the documentary chronicles the history of Vienna's Prater park, home to the landmark Riesenrad ferris wheel, from its origins as Habsburg hunting grounds to its present life as a popular amusement site. Director Ulrike Ottinger focuses on the generations of people who built, ran and worked the park's attractions. The film won the German Film Critics Award for Best Documentary in 2008 and is screened here as part of an Ottinger retrospective.

15246.one_liner: A Japanese horror-comedy in which a mysterious, disheveled woman in pink becomes an urban legend after young men at an art school start dying at the hands of a vengeful ex-girlfriend.
15246.long_desc: At an art academy, male students begin dying under strange circumstances, and rumor attributes the killings to a wild, unkempt woman in pink who is targeting men who wronged her romantically. The film mixes graphic J-horror violence with absurdist romantic comedy, drawn loosely from the director's own dating experiences. It is the feature directorial debut of Japanese comedian Retriever Yuriyan, produced by Hirokazu Kore-eda, Takashi Miike and Shunji Iwai, and won Best Film at the 2025 Monsters - Fantastic Film Festival. Contains strobing lights.

15384.one_liner: An Australian body-horror satire about a medical student who starts making a weight-loss drug from stolen human remains, with grotesque side effects.
15384.long_desc: Hana, a medical student desperate to impress her fitness instructor, discovers a highly effective weight-loss substance derived from human remains and gains access to a morgue to keep producing it for herself. The pounds come off fast, but the treatment triggers increasingly disturbing physical side effects. Directed by Natalie Erika James (2026, Australia) and starring Midori Francis, the film follows in the body-horror/satire vein of The Substance, skewering contemporary beauty standards and Ozempic-era weight-loss culture.

15237.one_liner: A Finnish-led supernatural horror film about a couple who move into an old house in the woods to raise their first child, only to find the home and forest harboring something malevolent.
15237.long_desc: An expectant couple relocates to a decaying house surrounded by forest, hoping to raise their child close to nature, but the house's disturbing history and the wild forest around it begin threatening their plans. The film uses supernatural horror to explore new-parent anxiety and the pressures of family life. Directed by Hanna Bergholm (her English-language debut, following Hatching), it stars Seidi Haarla and Rupert Grint and competed for the Golden Bear at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival.

15385.one_liner: A French-Italian crime thriller in which an unstable police officer transferred to a small town plagued by a wild boar invasion investigates a farmer's disappearance, unsure if it's animal or human violence.
15385.long_desc: Officer Fulda, emotionally unstable and newly reassigned to a rural French town overrun by wild boars, is paired with visiting psychologist Stéphane to look into a farmer's disappearance. Their investigation must determine whether the man fell victim to the boars or to hunters profiting from the crisis, uncovering the town's darker secrets along the way. The film mixes murder-mystery plotting with drug-fueled, absurdist detours and eccentric characters. Directed by Sarah Arnold (France/Italy, 2026) and starring Alexis Manenti, it won the Label Europa Cinemas award at Cannes 2026.

15210.one_liner: The 1986 musical comedy-horror film about a put-upon flower shop clerk whose strange new plant turns out to be a talking, blood-hungry alien bent on world domination.
15210.long_desc: Seymour, a shy botanist working at a failing flower shop, discovers an unusual plant during a solar eclipse and names it Audrey II after a coworker he has a crush on. The plant draws crowds to the shop but turns out to be a sentient, carnivorous creature from outer space that demands human blood and has designs on taking over the world. Directed by Frank Oz and based on the off-Broadway musical (itself adapted from Roger Corman's 1960 film), it features supporting turns from John Candy, Bill Murray, Christopher Guest and James Belushi. This screening is the director's cut, and the film won a Saturn Award for Best Music.
